items.stem: A PM is pushed to 'add AI' to boost marketing appeal. What should drive the decision instead?

options.text: Whether AI meaningfully solves a real user problem better than alternatives
options.rationale: Correct: user value and fit should drive the decision, not hype.

options.text: Whether competitors mention AI in their ads
options.rationale: Competitor marketing is not a sound basis for a feature.

options.text: Whether the word 'AI' will impress investors
Whether it is the newest technology available

items.explanation: Correct: user value and fit should drive the decision, not hype.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO design choices handle AI uncertainty responsibly in a product? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Provide a clear fallback when the AI response is low-confidence or fails
options.rationale: Correct: fallbacks protect the user experience when AI errs.

options.text: Let users review or correct AI output before it acts
options.rationale: Correct: human review limits the impact of AI errors.

options.text: Hide all errors and present output as always correct
options.rationale: Hiding errors misleads users and erodes trust.

options.text: Assume the model is always right at launch
options.rationale: Assuming perfection ignores real failure modes.

items.explanation: Correct: fallbacks protect the user experience when AI errs.

items.stem: Why must a PM consider inference cost early when scoping an AI feature?

options.text: Per-request costs can make a feature unviable at scale
options.rationale: Correct: cost and latency at scale can break the business case.
Running models typically has a real per-use cost.
Unplanned costs can sink a feature after launch.

items.explanation: Correct: cost and latency at scale can break the business case.
